Hi John & Sarah,

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier — great discussion. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Recap / priorities (from our call)
- Latency: target p50 < 120ms, p95 < 250ms for user-facing completions
- Quality: unchanged for critical summarization flows (no regressions)
- Cost: looking to reduce TCO vs current hosted vendor by ~30% for inference spend
- Ops: requirement for audit logs and SSO; potential Dedicated capacity later this quarter

Immediate next steps I propose:
1) We run a 24–72 hour evaluation using your real prompt-set (you mentioned ~2k seed prompts). We’ll produce per-prompt quality metrics + token cost.
2) We’ll deliver a short model shortlist and rationale (cost / latency / quality tradeoffs).
3) Recommend A/B evaluation plan and target success metrics.

I’ve attached our initial benchmark export (acme-mvp-benchmarks.csv) and a zip of the prompt sets you shared (acme-prompt-sets.zip). Please confirm the prompt set version — I used the file Sarah uploaded in Drive earlier today.

Hi John / Sarah — thanks for the quick pass on prompts; we removed the PII items you flagged and kicked off the eval this morning. Below is the recommended shortlist based on your quality targets, latency constraints, and cost goals. I included rationale and a suggested A/B plan. The attached spreadsheet (acme-model-shortlist.xlsx) has per-model eval results + token cost estimates.

Recommended shortlist (ranked)
1) redwood-optim-7b-8bit
   - Rationale: best balance of latency and cost for interactive UIs. In our small-scale eval it produced parity-level quality on summarization prompts vs the higher-capacity baseline but at ~45% lower per-token cost. P50 latency (hosted) ~80–110ms; p95 ~220–260ms depending on sequence length.
2) open-llama-13b-4bit (quantized)
   - Rationale: noticeably better on long-context summarization and edge cases; higher compute but better factuality on the prompt set. Per-token cost ~1.6x of 7b option; p50 latency ~150–190ms. Good candidate for an offline heavy path or for customer-facing flows where quality is critical.
3) gptx-3.5-ref (licensed)
   - Rationale: highest quality on narrow NLU tasks in our eval, but licensing + cost is materially higher. Considered as fallback or for critical flows only.

Tradeoffs & notes
- If your priority is strict latency for interactive features, start with redwood-optim-7b-8bit and run a canary for the highest-traffic route.
- If you need the best absolute quality on edge summarization, run a controlled eval of open-llama-13b-4bit and monitor hallucination rates closely (we saw slight improvements vs 7b on factuality but with higher cost).
- Dedicated capacity changes the unit economics — we can model Dedicated vs Hosted in the attached sheet; for your concurrency profile Dedicated becomes attractive at sustained capacity > 40 RPS.

Suggested A/B evaluation plan
- A/B (50/50) on 5k production-like requests across your top 3 flows for 48 hours. Track precision/factuality, latency percentiles, and token cost.
- Pass/fail metric: no regression in summary accuracy (>98% of seed prompts within existing quality delta), and p95 latency < 300ms.

Links & artifacts
- Eval results (spreadsheet): acme-model-shortlist.xlsx (attached)
- Full raw export: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C_acme-evals
- Prompt sets & scoring docs: https://docs.redwood.com/evals/acme/prompt-sets
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/1234567/ACME-2026-042

Next steps

Thanks — I’ll loop in Solutions if we get the go-ahead.

Quick technical note from my side after looking at the initial eval export: 

- The numbers in acme-mvp-benchmarks.csv line up with what Marissa summarized. For your typical 256-token completion profile:
  * redwood-optim-7b-8bit -> estimated hosted cost ~$0.90 per 1k tokens; p50 ~95ms (EU/US regions), p95 ~240ms
  * open-llama-13b-4bit -> estimated hosted cost ~$1.45 per 1k tokens; p50 ~165ms, p95 ~310ms
  * gptx-3.5-ref -> estimated hosted cost ~$2.8 per 1k tokens; p50 ~120ms (but higher variance)

- Dedicated math: if you commit to a Dedicated pool sized for 60 RPS we can drop per-token unit cost for 7b by ~30% vs hosted while guaranteeing p95 < 250ms with proper batching and KV cache policies. We’ll model Dedicated vs Hosted in the spreadsheet (tab: "unit_econ").

- Hallucinations: open-llama-13b showed fewer hallucination cases in the seed prompts we sampled, but variance increases on longer contexts. Recommend adding a small fact-checker step (reranking with a lightweight verifier model) for the top-3% failure modes during the A/B run.

Operational asks for the A/B run (we can take these on):
1) Provide production-like traffic sample (5k requests) and we’ll replay against the shortlisted models.
2) We need API keys for any external licensed models you want included (e.g., gptx).
3) Agree on rollback thresholds (we suggest immediate rollback if p95 > 400ms or quality regression >3% on seed prompts).

Happy to jump on a quick call Wed morning to finalize the run details.

—David Kim
Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
david_kim@redwood.com

Note: attachment acme-model-shortlist.xlsx contains per-model latency/cost breakdowns and the Dedicated vs Hosted unit-econ tab.
